ranking_metric: deps.dev directDependentCount summed over all releases
uncertainty: Pilot cell: five JVM paths verified, netty-codec-dns, dnsjava, pcap4j-core, minidns-core and the Scala library dns4s-core_2.13, ranked by deps.dev direct dependents summed over releases (a weak signal; Pcap4J's count covers its whole multi-protocol artifact). Scala libraries count in this Java cell when they document a JVM API, as Scala and Kotlin libraries such as circe-yaml and ktoml do in other Java cells; dns4s is ranked by its Scala 2.13 coordinate only. Netty leaves A/AAAA as raw records (the harness formats the decoded bytes) and its DnsQuery has no AA/TC/RA/RCODE. Pcap4J's names come from DnsDomainName.decompress, whose leading '.' for pointer-only names the harness drops, and its coverage and AFL++ feedback are scoped to its DNS classes. MiniDNS decodes AD and CD but not the reserved Z bit; dns4s decodes none of Z, AD and CD. Round 2 added targeted deps.dev lookups for the plausible Maven search hits: the Netty backport and Netty 5 alpha are the selected Netty family, ph-dns and spotify dns wrap dnsjava, happy-dns keeps its parser package-private, and ninio-dns and the Direct Project DNS are network applications. Each verified path parses the two valid controls (a query and a response with compressed CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers) to the hand-written oracle summary, has library source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback that differs between the controls. Two valid controls do not establish EDNS0, DNSSEC, TXT, authority/additional or malformed-input behaviour. Package-level adoption metrics include non-DNS use, and the cell is not a definitive top ten.
selection: Five control-verified Java DNS path(s), ranked by deps.dev directDependentCount summed over all releases: netty-codec-dns 4.2.21.Final (1,038), dnsjava 3.7.1 (888), pcap4j-core 1.8.2 (210), minidns-core 1.1.3 (32), dns4s-core_2.13 0.21.0 (22).
